steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
With a few sentences, you'll make several files, move them into a folder and rename them all at once.

Today you'll learn three new things.

  1. Have it make several files at once
  2. Have it make a folder, move and rename files
  3. How to read a new permission card: "May I run this command?"
  • Time: 15 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 3
Today you'll move files, so be sure to work only inside the Practice folder.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html:
It's a new job, so start a new chat. (You learned this in Desktop 3!)

  1. Claude app → Code tab → + New at the top left.
  2. Check that the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual. It matters today: in other modes it may make folders and move files without asking.

steps.title: Make 3 memo files at once
steps.html: Send the sentence below. As in Desktop 1, a create-file permission card appears once per file, three times. Check each file name and click Allow each time.
steps.alt: Three memo files appear in the Practice folder
steps.code: Create 3 memo files, meeting.txt, groceries.txt and ideas.txt, with a line or two of example text in each

check.q: Did you allow all three, and are there 3 new files in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If some files are missing
steps.html:
• If you denied any card, that file wasn't made. Say "Also make the files you haven't made yet."
  • If the folder window was already open, close it and open it again.
  • It may have asked just once for all of them. If the 3 files are there, you're fine.

steps.title: First, what's a 'command'?
steps.html:
So far Claude has created and edited the contents of files.

Making folders and moving files works a little differently. Claude gives your computer a short instruction in English (a command). So this time a different permission card appears: May I run this command?

mkdirmake a folder
mvmove or rename

You don't need to memorize commands. The next step shows how to read the card.

steps.title: Make a folder and move the files
steps.html: Send the sentence below. A new run-command permission card appears. Don't click yet; just compare it with the picture.
steps.alt: A permission card showing the command to run and its description
steps.code: Make a memos folder and move the three files you just made into it

check.q: Did a permission card with a command and a description appear, like the picture?

steps.title: If it did it without asking
steps.html:
The permission mode probably wasn't Manual. In Accept edits mode, common file commands like making folders and moving files run without asking.

  • Click the permission mode button under the typing box and switch to Manual.
  • If the files have already moved, you can practise with the card in the next step (renaming).

choices.label: Show how to read the card

steps.title: How to read the 'May I run this command?' card
steps.html:
Title at the topA card asking to run a command (Run command, Bash, etc.)
English in the dark boxThe actual command it will run
Description belowWhat Claude says it's going to do. Read this part
Allow / DenyRun it / don't

You don't need to understand the command. Just check that the description matches what you asked. If it does, click Allow.

Stop if you see these. rm, del and Remove-Item are commands that delete. If you didn't ask to delete anything, click Deny.
Even if you see a button like 'Always allow', don't click it for now.

check.q: Did the description match your request, and did you click Allow?

steps.title: If the description doesn't match or is confusing
steps.html:
• That's exactly when to click Deny. Nothing changes.
  • Then ask again, e.g. "Just make a memos folder and move the meeting, groceries and ideas files into it. Don't delete anything."
  • If there are several commands, it may ask several times. Read the description each time.

steps.title: Rename all the files at once
steps.html:
Now add today's date to the front of the three file names. The run-command permission card appears again. Read the description and click Allow if it matches.

The real date today is used.
steps.code: Add today's date to the front of the file names in the memos folder, e.g. 2026-11-23_meeting.txt

check.q: Did you read the description and click Allow?

steps.title: Check the result yourself
steps.html:
1. Open the Practice folder on your desktop. There's a new memos folder.
  2. Double-click the memos folder to open it.

If the 3 files are inside with the date in front of their names, it worked.
steps.alt: Three files with dates in their names inside the memos folder

check.q: Are there 3 files with dates in their names in the memos folder?

steps.title: If the result looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder window was already open, close it and open it again.
  • If something moved to the wrong place or got an odd name, tell Claude "Undo what you just did." Read the permission card then too.
  • You can also ask Claude, "What's in the memos folder now?"

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop practice 4 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Something that would have meant moving and renaming files one by one took just a few sentences.

Your requestClaude turns it into commandsRun-command cardread, then AllowFolder tidied

Three things to remember

  1. Several files can be created, moved and renamed with a single sentence.
  2. Making folders, moving and renaming ask through a run-command permission card.
  3. You don't need to know the commands; read the description. Be extra careful with delete commands (rm, del).

Next step

You clicked a lot of permission cards today, right? In the next practice you'll learn to change this permission mode, and when it's safe to do so.
